title: Your first terraform apply: a resource group and a storage account

ticket.subject: Sensors platform: a dev resource group, in code from day one
body: We start the sensors platform this sprint and I want it in Terraform from the first resource. `main.tf` only
has the provider for now. Please add:
- **A resource group** `azurerm_resource_group.main`, named `rg-sensors-<env>`, in the region given by a
- **A variable `env`** (a `string`) that only accepts `dev`, `test` or `prod` (a `validation` block), and is
- **A storage account** `azurerm_storage_account.raw` for the raw sensor files, named `stsensorsraw<env>01`,
Standard, LRS, TLS 1.2 at least, in the same resource group and region (refer to the resource group, do not
- **An output `resource_group_id`**: the network team needs the id for a role assignment.
Our dev environment lives in **North Europe** (`northeurope`): put the values for dev in `terraform.tfvars`,
not in the code. Run `terraform plan` and read it before you apply; afterwards a new plan must show nothing to
This is the lab's simulated subscription: nothing is created in Azure.

hints: `terraform init` once (it installs the provider), then `terraform plan`: read the "+ create" lines and the summary "Plan: 2 to add" before `terraform apply`.

A resource block is `resource "<type>" "<name>" { ... }`; other blocks refer to it as `<type>.<name>.<attribute>`, for example `azurerm_resource_group.main.name`. The reference also tells Terraform which one to create first.
Inside a string, `"rg-sensors-${var.env}"` inserts a variable. A `validation { condition = contains(["dev", "test", "prod"], var.env) error_message = "..." }` block refuses other values.
Terraform reads `terraform.tfvars` automatically: one `name = value` line per variable. A variable without a default and without a value makes `plan` fail.
A `locals { tags = { ... } }` block avoids repeating the tags: `tags = local.tags`.
`terraform output` prints the outputs after an apply; `terraform state list` shows what Terraform manages.
